newsitem.title: USA: Pall Corp blames forex rates for dip in net.
newsitem.headline: Pall Corp blames forex rates for dip in net.

text.p: Pall Corp said that in the second quarter ended Feb 1 sales were flat on a unit and price basis with a reduction of 2 percent because of foreign currency exchange rates.
All of the reduction was due to exchange rates, which hurt sales 2-1/2 percent.
The company said it announced this would happen last January.
By market segment, before the effects of exchange rates, Health Care was down 3 percent, Aeropower grew 7 percent and Fluid Processing was down 1/2 percent.

It said that all that changed compared to expectations was that Microelectronics improved with a late rush of business so that it was only down 8 percent in volume, but Europe, instead of being flat, was down 5 percent.
The company said that in health care sub-segments in local currency, it saw continued growth in pharmaceuticals, which grew 7.5 percent.
"This was led by Asia which grew 34 percent and the U.S. which grew 21 percent, but Europe was down 5 percent." Chairman and Chief Executive Eric Krasnoff said in a statement.
Food and Beverage was up 15 percent, which included 20 percent growth in Asia. Patient Protection decreased 7 percent and BioSupport fell 36 percent, it said.

"Patient Protection was of more concern and breaking this out by geography, the U.S. was down 8 percent, Europe was down 16 percent and Asia grew 19 percent," Krasnoff said. "Breaking it down further, blood filter sales overall were down 4 percent, including a reduction of 3 percent related to pricing."
